title: Ghost Nebula, vdB 141
caption: The Ghost Nebula (vdB 141), imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) & H. Schweiker (WIYN)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Several stars are embedded in vdB 141, a reflection nebula in the constellation Cepheus, and their light gives it a ghoulish brown color. It is sometimes called the Ghost Nebula.
Its less memorable official name comes from a catalog. vdB 141 is its number in Sidney van den Bergh's list of reflection nebulae, published in 1966.

A reflection nebula does not glow on its own. Instead, clouds of dust scatter and reflect the light of nearby stars, so the nebula's color depends on both the stars and the dust. Because the stars that light vdB 141 are embedded inside it, the dust is illuminated from within rather than from the side. Its brownish tint shows that a reflection nebula need not be blue.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope recorded this through B, V, I and hydrogen-alpha filters. The source does not say which color each filter was assigned.
filters: 438 nm · Optical B (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)

understand.eye: The nebula is too faint for the eye. Long exposures reveal its dusty glow, and the I filter records near-infrared light.
